title: Continuity at a Point: The Three Conditions
quickIdea: f is continuous at a when f(a) is defined, the two-sided limit exists, and the two are equal.
remember: f is continuous at x = a when lim(x->a) f(x) = f(a).
Unpacked into three checks: f(a) must exist; lim(x->a) f(x) must exist, which needs LHL = RHL; and the limit must equal f(a).
Failure of any one of the three is a discontinuity, and which one failed tells you the type.
Sums, differences, products and quotients of continuous functions are continuous, the quotient only where the denominator is non-zero.
A composition of continuous functions is continuous, which is why polynomials, sin, cos, e^x and ln x can be combined freely on their domains.
On a closed interval [a, b] continuity at the endpoints means one-sided continuity: RHL = f(a) at a, and LHL = f(b) at b.

example.prompt: Is the function of GATE CSE 2013 Q.22 option (A) continuous at x = 3? It is f(x) = (x + 3)/3 for x < 3, f(x) = x - 1 for x > 3, and f(3) = 2.
example.work: LHL: (3 + 3)/3 = 2. RHL: 3 - 1 = 2. Function value: f(3) = 2. All three quantities are 2.
example.answer: Yes. LHL = RHL = f(3) = 2, so the function is continuous at 3 - and it is the only option of the four that is.

gateAngle: 2013 Q.22 offers four piecewise functions and asks which is continuous at 3; three fail in three different ways (removable, jump, infinite). 2026 Set 1 Q.22 supplies f(0) = 3 and a formula valid for x > 0, and asks for c1 + c2 so that the one-sided limit at 0 equals 3. Both questions are decided by the same three checks.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: For f(x) = 2x + 1 when x < 3 and f(x) = 3x - 2 when x >= 3, is f continuous at x = 3?
variations.why: The smallest version of the GATE shape: two linear pieces that happen to meet. Change one coefficient and the same computation produces a jump.

variations.label: CONCEPTUAL PRACTICE QUESTION
variations.question: If lim(x->a) f(x) exists, must f be continuous at a?
variations.answer: No. Continuity also needs the limit to equal f(a). With f(x) = 5 for x not equal to 3 and f(3) = 4, the limit at 3 exists and equals 5, yet f is discontinuous at 3.
variations.why: This is the distinction 2013 Q.22 option (B) is built on. Existence of the limit and continuity are not the same condition.

variations.label: PREDICTED VARIATION
variations.question: Find c so that f(x) = c e^x - 2 ln(1/x) for x > 0 and f(x) = 3 otherwise is continuous at x = 0, given that the logarithmic term must vanish.
variations.answer: The term -2 ln(1/x) = 2 ln x tends to -infinity as x -> 0+, so no finite c repairs it unless its coefficient is 0. With the coefficient 0 the one-sided limit is c, so c = 3.
variations.why: This is GATE CSE 2026 Set 1 Q.22's reasoning: a term that blows up cannot be balanced by a constant, so its coefficient must be forced to zero before the remaining constant is matched.

trap.what: Checking only that the limit exists, or only that the two one-sided limits agree, and declaring continuity.
trap.why: Continuity is a three-part condition. A function can have a perfectly good limit at a and still fail to be continuous there because f(a) is defined differently or not at all.
trap.counterexample: f(x) = 8 - x for x not equal to 3 with f(3) = 4: both one-sided limits are 5, so the limit exists, but 5 is not 4 and f is discontinuous. That is option (B) of GATE CSE 2013 Q.22.

check.question: Is f(x) = (x^2 - 9)/(x - 3) for x not equal to 3, with f(3) = 6, continuous at 3?
check.explanation: The limit at 3 is 6 because the expression equals x + 3 away from 3, and f(3) is defined as 6, so all three conditions hold. Had f(3) been left undefined or set to any other number, the function would be discontinuous.
